crops.name: Tomatoes
crops.description: The garden staple. Warm-season fruiting vines that want heat, even water, and a sturdy cage.
crops.plantingTips: Set out after the last frost when nights stay above 10°C. Bury the stem up to the first true leaves so extra roots form.
crops.spacing: 45–60 cm between plants, 90 cm between rows
crops.pests: Hornworms, aphids, early blight, blossom-end rot
crops.feeding: Compost at planting. Side-dress with a balanced feed when the first fruit sets, then every two weeks.
careSteps: Harden off seedlings for a week.
Stake or cage when plants reach 20 cm.
Water at the soil, not the leaves.
Pick when fully colored and slightly soft.

crops.name: Lettuce
crops.description: A cool-weather leaf crop that bolts in heat. Sow little and often for a steady salad bowl.
crops.soilType: Loose, fertile soil with steady moisture
crops.plantingTips: Sow directly as soon as the soil can be worked. Shade cloth in late spring keeps leaves sweet.
crops.feeding: A light compost tea every two weeks. Avoid high nitrogen once heads begin to fill.
careSteps: Sow every 10–14 days for a succession.
Keep soil evenly moist to prevent bitterness.
Harvest outer leaves or cut the whole head at the base.
Stop sowing when nights stay above 20°C.

crops.name: Carrots
crops.description: Sweet roots that need stone-free soil and patience. Thin early so shoulders can swell.
crops.plantingTips: Sow directly — carrots resent transplanting. Keep the seedbed damp until germination, which can take two weeks.
crops.pests: Carrot fly, wireworms, forked roots in compacted soil
crops.feeding: Little extra feed if the bed was composted. Too much nitrogen grows tops, not roots.
careSteps: Sow shallow and thin to a finger-width.
Hill soil over shoulders to stop greening.
Water deeply once a week.
Harvest when crowns are 2 cm across.

crops.name: Peppers
crops.description: Heat lovers that fruit for months once nights are warm. Both sweet bells and hot chiles follow the same care.
crops.plantingTips: Start indoors 8 weeks before last frost. Do not rush them outside — cold nights stall growth for weeks.
crops.feeding: Balanced feed until flowers, then a potassium-rich feed to set fruit.
careSteps: Transplant only when nights stay above 12°C.
Mulch to keep roots warm and even.
Pick often to keep plants producing.
Leave the last fruit to color fully before frost.

crops.name: Cucumbers
crops.description: Fast vines that drink a lot and crop heavily in heat. A trellis keeps fruit straight and leaves dry.
crops.plantingTips: Sow or set out after soil is truly warm. Cold, wet ground invites damping-off.
crops.spacing: 40 cm on a trellis, 90 cm if sprawling
crops.pests: Cucumber beetles, powdery mildew, bitter fruit from drought
crops.feeding: Compost at planting and a weekly dilute feed once vines run.
careSteps: Train vines up a trellis.
Water deeply at the base every morning in heat.
Harvest at 15–20 cm for slicing types.
Remove yellowing leaves to slow mildew.

crops.name: Beans
crops.description: Bush or pole legumes that feed the soil as they grow. Direct-sow once frost is gone.
crops.soilType: Average, well-drained soil — not too rich
crops.plantingTips: Do not soak seed in cold soil. Wait until the ground is warm to the touch.
crops.spacing: 10 cm for bush, 20 cm for pole
crops.feeding: Skip heavy nitrogen. A handful of compost at sowing is enough.
careSteps: Sow succession crops every three weeks.
Provide a pole or net for climbers.
Pick pods young to keep plants flowering.
Leave a few pods to dry for next year’s seed.

crops.name: Spinach
crops.description: A short, cool-season green that melts in heat. Best in late winter and again in autumn.
crops.plantingTips: Sow thickly in cool soil. Long days plus heat trigger bolting — harvest promptly.
crops.feeding: A nitrogen-rich compost tea once after thinning.
careSteps: Sow as soon as soil thaws.
Keep evenly moist.
Cut outer leaves or harvest whole plants.
Resow in late summer for a fall crop.

crops.name: Zucchini
crops.description: One or two plants feed a household. Harvest small and often or they become clubs overnight.
crops.plantingTips: Sow after frost in hills of rich soil. Give them room — leaves spread fast.
crops.pests: Squash bugs, powdery mildew, blossom-end rot
crops.feeding: Compost at planting, then a light weekly feed while fruiting.
careSteps: Plant in hills of two or three seeds, thin to the strongest.
Water at the crown, not the leaves.
Pick at 15–20 cm.
Remove mildewed leaves promptly.

crops.name: Corn
crops.description: A wind-pollinated grass. Plant in blocks, not a single row, or cobs will be half-filled.
crops.plantingTips: Sow when soil is at least 16°C. Hill soil around stems as they grow.
crops.spacing: 25–30 cm in blocks of at least 4×4
crops.feeding: Heavy feeder: compost before sowing and side-dress when plants are knee-high.
careSteps: Sow in a block for pollination.
Water deeply as silks appear.
Harvest when silks brown and kernels squirt milky juice.
Leave stalks for beans to climb if you like.

crops.name: Radishes
crops.description: The fastest crop in the bed. Perfect for filling gaps and marking slow carrot rows.
crops.plantingTips: Sow every two weeks in cool weather. Heat makes them pithy and hot.
crops.pests: Flea beetles, root maggots, splitting from uneven water
crops.feeding: No extra feed needed in decent soil.
careSteps: Sow shallow and thin early.
Keep evenly moist.
Harvest at 2–3 cm across.
Eat the greens too.

crops.name: Broccoli
crops.description: A cool-season brassica. Heads form in spring; heat makes them bolt to yellow flowers.
crops.plantingTips: Start indoors or sow in late winter. Firm the soil around stems so they do not rock.
crops.feeding: Compost plus a nitrogen feed until heads appear, then ease off.
careSteps: Net against cabbage moths.
Keep soil moist and cool with mulch.
Cut the main head with a short stem.
Leave the plant — side shoots often follow.

crops.name: Pumpkin
crops.description: Long-season vines that want heat, space, and a rich hill. One plant can cover a bed.
crops.plantingTips: Sow after frost on a compost mound. Set fruit on a tile or board to keep the skin clean.
crops.feeding: A shovelful of compost in the hill and a monthly feed while fruit swells.
careSteps: Pinch extra fruit if you want larger pumpkins.
Water deeply at the root, not the fruit.
Cure in sun for 10 days after harvest.
Store cool and dry.

crops.name: Kale
crops.description: The hardiest brassica. Frost sweetens the leaves; summer heat makes them tough.
crops.plantingTips: Sow in late winter or late summer. Pick leaf by leaf from the bottom up.
crops.feeding: Compost at planting and a light nitrogen feed after each heavy pick.
careSteps: Net young plants against moths.
Mulch to keep roots cool.
Harvest lower leaves first.
Leave the crown growing for months.

crops.name: Eggplant
crops.description: A tropical nightshade that sulks in cold. Once nights are warm it fruits steadily.
crops.plantingTips: Start indoors and wait for truly warm soil. Black plastic mulch helps in cooler zones.
crops.pests: Flea beetles, spider mites, verticillium wilt
crops.feeding: Compost at planting, then a fortnightly feed once flowers open.
careSteps: Transplant only when nights stay above 15°C.
Stake heavy-fruited types.
Pick while the skin is glossy.
Dull skin means the fruit is over-mature.

crops.name: Green Onions
crops.description: Bunching onions you can snip for months. Sow thickly and treat as a cut-and-come-again herb.
crops.plantingTips: Direct-sow almost any cool stretch of the year. They tolerate light frost.
crops.feeding: A light compost tea once a month.
careSteps: Sow every three weeks for a constant supply.
Keep evenly moist.
Cut 2 cm above the soil and let them regrow.
Divide clumps in the second year.

crops.name: Beets
crops.description: Roots and greens in one sowing. Soak seed overnight — each ‘seed’ is a cluster.
crops.soilType: Loose, stone-free soil, not freshly manured
crops.plantingTips: Sow directly in cool soil. Thin clusters so roots can swell; eat the thinnings.
crops.pests: Leaf miners, scab, woody roots in heat
crops.feeding: Skip extra nitrogen. Compost worked in before sowing is enough.
careSteps: Soak seed overnight.
Thin to one plant per station.
Keep evenly moist to avoid zoning.
Harvest at golf-ball to tennis-ball size.

crops.name: Cabbage
crops.description: A slow, cool brassica that needs firm soil and steady water to make a tight head.
crops.plantingTips: Start indoors 6 weeks before last frost, or sow for a fall crop in midsummer.
crops.feeding: Compost plus a nitrogen feed until heading, then water only.
careSteps: Plant firmly so stems do not wobble.
Net against moths.
Water evenly to stop heads splitting.
Cut at the base when the head feels solid.

crops.name: Cauliflower
crops.description: The fussiest brassica. It wants cool, even weather and a blanching leaf tied over the curd.
crops.plantingTips: Transplant into rich soil and never let it dry out — stress makes button heads.
crops.feeding: Steady feeding until the curd appears, then water only.
careSteps: Keep growth never-stopping.
Tie inner leaves over the curd when it is egg-sized.
Harvest while the curd is tight and white.
Do not wait — it goes ricey fast.

crops.name: Garlic
crops.description: A long crop planted in autumn and lifted in early summer. Cloves need a cold spell to divide.
crops.plantingTips: Plant individual cloves point-up, 5 cm deep, after the soil cools but before hard freeze.
crops.spacing: 12–15 cm between cloves, 25 cm between rows
crops.feeding: Compost at planting. No extra feed in spring unless leaves yellow.
careSteps: Plant the largest cloves.
Mulch after the ground chills.
Cut scapes on hardneck types when they curl.
Lift when half the leaves have browned; cure two weeks.

crops.name: Onions
crops.description: Long-day types for northern summers, short-day for the south. Sets are easier than seed.
crops.plantingTips: Plant sets in early spring with the tip just showing. Keep weeds down — onions hate competition.
crops.pests: Thrips, onion maggot, neck rot in wet harvests
crops.feeding: A nitrogen feed until bulbs swell, then stop so necks can dry.
careSteps: Plant sets 2 cm deep.
Water steadily until tops fall.
Stop watering when necks soften.
Cure in a dry, airy place for two weeks.

crops.name: Peas
crops.description: A cool-season climber. Sow as soon as the soil can be worked; heat ends the crop.
crops.plantingTips: Sow thickly along a trellis. Inoculant helps in new beds.
crops.spacing: 5 cm apart along a net or pea sticks
crops.pests: Aphids, powdery mildew, birds on seedlings
crops.feeding: No nitrogen. A little potash if flowers are shy.
careSteps: Sow in late winter.
Provide a net the day they sprout.
Pick pods every other day.
Water at flowering for a fuller crop.

crops.name: Potatoes
crops.description: Grown from seed tubers, not true seed. Hill soil as they grow to keep tubers in the dark.
crops.soilType: Loose, slightly acidic, never freshly limed
crops.plantingTips: Plant chitted tubers when soil is 8°C. Frost blackens tops — cover if a late freeze threatens.
crops.feeding: Compost in the trench. Avoid high nitrogen after flowering.
careSteps: Chit tubers in light for two weeks.
Hill when stems are 15 cm tall.
Water well from flowering onward.
Lift new potatoes two weeks after flowers; maincrop when tops die.

crops.name: Swiss Chard
crops.description: A beet grown for leaves. Heat-tolerant enough to bridge the gap when spinach bolts.
crops.plantingTips: Sow in spring and again in late summer. Harvest outer stems so the crown keeps producing.
crops.feeding: Compost at sowing and a monthly nitrogen feed while picking.
careSteps: Sow directly or transplant.
Keep soil moist.
Twist outer stems off at the base.
A light frost sweetens the leaves.

crops.name: Okra
crops.description: A heat-loving hibiscus. Pods go from perfect to woody in a day — pick every morning.
crops.plantingTips: Soak seed and sow only when nights stay above 16°C. It sulks in cool soil.
crops.feeding: Compost at planting, then a light monthly feed.
careSteps: Wait for real heat before sowing.
Harvest pods at 5–8 cm.
Wear gloves if stems irritate skin.
Keep picking or the plant stops.

crops.name: Strawberries
crops.description: A perennial bed that fruits in year one from runners. June-bearers peak once; everbearers trickle all summer.
crops.plantingTips: Plant crowns at soil level — too deep and they rot, too high and they dry. Mulch with straw.
crops.pests: Slugs, birds, grey mold, vine weevil
crops.feeding: Compost in spring. A potassium feed as flowers open.
careSteps: Plant with the crown exactly at soil level.
Pinch first-year flowers on everbearers if you want a stronger plant.
Net against birds.
Refresh the bed with new runners every three years.

crops.name: Watermelon
crops.description: A long, hot crop. One or two fruits per vine ripen better than a crowd.
crops.plantingTips: Sow in hills after soil is 21°C. Give vines a full bed in the sun.
crops.pests: Cucumber beetles, anthracnose, bland fruit from too much water at the end
crops.feeding: Compost in the hill. Ease off water as fruit near ripeness so sugars concentrate.
careSteps: Sow or transplant into warm soil.
Pinch to two fruits per vine.
A hollow sound and a dry tendril mean ripe.
Cut with a short stem attached.

crops.name: Cantaloupe
crops.description: Muskmelons that slip from the vine when ready. They need heat and a dry finish.
crops.plantingTips: Same as watermelon: warm soil, a rich hill, and full sun. Elevate fruit on a tile.
crops.feeding: Compost at planting; potassium as fruit swell; less water in the last week.
careSteps: Wait for heat.
Mulch to keep fruit clean.
Harvest when the stem slips with a gentle tug.
Eat within a few days — they do not store.

crops.name: Blueberries
crops.description: A long-lived shrub that must have acidic soil. Plant two varieties for a fuller crop.
crops.soilType: Acidic (pH 4.5–5.5), sandy, high in organic matter
crops.plantingTips: Set bare-root or potted bushes in early spring. Never lime the bed.
crops.pests: Birds, mummy berry, chlorosis in alkaline soil
crops.feeding: Acid fertilizer in early spring. Mulch with pine needles or bark.
careSteps: Test pH before planting.
Keep the root zone moist, never waterlogged.
Net as berries color.
Prune old canes in late winter from year three.

crops.name: Raspberries
crops.description: Canes that fruit on old wood (summer) or new wood (autumn). A post-and-wire row keeps them tidy.
crops.plantingTips: Plant canes in early spring 5 cm deeper than they grew in the nursery. Water in well.
crops.spacing: 40 cm in a row, 1.5 m between rows
crops.feeding: Compost in spring. Do not overfeed nitrogen or you get leaves, not berries.
careSteps: Plant on a wire support.
Mulch thickly.
For summer types, cut fruited canes to the ground after harvest.
Net as color comes on.

crops.name: Grapes
crops.description: A vine that wants a hot wall or a proper trellis and a winter prune. Crop comes from last year’s wood.
crops.soilType: Well-drained, even poor, slightly alkaline soil
crops.plantingTips: Plant dormant vines in early spring. Year one is for roots, not fruit — pinch bunches off.
crops.pests: Powdery mildew, birds, wasps on ripe bunches
crops.feeding: Little feed. Too much nitrogen makes sappy growth that mildews.
careSteps: Plant against a south wall or on wires.
Water the first summer, then sparingly.
Winter-prune to a few buds per spur.
Thin bunches if the vine over-sets.

crops.name: Figs
crops.description: A sun-baked wall shrub. In cool climates grow in a pot you can shelter in winter.
crops.plantingTips: Plant in spring in the warmest, driest spot you have. Restricting roots often improves fruiting.
crops.spacing: 3–4 m in open ground, or a 40 cm pot
crops.feeding: Almost none in the ground. Potted figs want a monthly feed from spring to midsummer.
careSteps: Choose a warm wall.
Water potted plants in summer drought.
Pinch new shoots to five leaves.
Pick when the neck droops and the fruit feels soft.

crops.name: Passion Fruit
crops.description: A vigorous tropical vine. It needs a strong trellis, water in the dry season, and a warm winter.
crops.plantingTips: Plant after frost against a fence. In the subtropics it fruits in 6–12 months.
crops.companions: Basil, beans — keep the root zone clear of heavy shade
crops.pests: Fruit flies, woodiness virus, snails on young shoots
crops.feeding: Compost in spring and a complete feed every six weeks in the growing season.
careSteps: Give a sturdy trellis from day one.
Water deeply in dry spells.
Hand-pollinate in still, closed greenhouses.
Pick when fruit colors and drops into a net.

crops.name: Basil
crops.description: The tomato’s companion. Pinch hard and it bushes; let it flower and the leaves turn tough.
crops.plantingTips: Sow or transplant after nights stay above 12°C. Cold blackens the leaves overnight.
crops.feeding: Compost at planting. A dilute liquid feed if leaves pale.
careSteps: Pinch above a leaf pair when 15 cm tall.
Never let it flower if you want leaves.
Water in the morning.
Take cuttings in late summer to pot up indoors.

crops.name: Cilantro
crops.description: A cool, short-lived herb. Heat sends it to seed (coriander) in a week. Sow often.
crops.plantingTips: Direct-sow — it hates transplanting. Choose a bolt-resistant variety for late spring.
crops.companions: Anise, spinach, tomatoes (as a trap for aphids)
crops.feeding: No extra feed. Rich soil makes sappy, fast-bolting plants.
careSteps: Sow every two weeks.
Keep cool and moist.
Cut stems at the base.
Leave a few plants to set coriander seed.

crops.name: Parsley
crops.description: A biennial you grow as an annual. Slow to germinate, then it cuts for months.
crops.plantingTips: Soak seed overnight. Be patient — two to three weeks is normal.
crops.pests: Carrot fly, leaf spot, swallowtail caterpillars (share a few)
crops.feeding: Compost at planting and a mid-season compost tea.
careSteps: Soak seed, then sow shallow.
Keep the seedbed damp.
Cut outer stems; leave the crown.
Replace plants in the second spring before they bolt.

crops.name: Mint
crops.description: A spreader. Plant it in a pot sunk in the bed or it will own the garden.
crops.plantingTips: Start from a rooted cutting, not seed, so you keep the flavor you wanted.
crops.companions: Cabbage, peas, tomatoes — in a pot beside them, not in their bed
crops.pests: Mint rust, flea beetles, runaway roots
crops.feeding: A compost mulch in spring. Cut back and it flushes again.
careSteps: Plant in a container.
Keep soil moist.
Cut often to keep leaves tender.
Divide every spring.

crops.name: Rosemary
crops.description: A woody Mediterranean shrub. Dry feet, full sun, and a sharp prune after flowering.
crops.soilType: Very well-drained, even poor, alkaline soil
crops.plantingTips: Buy a plant — seed is slow and unreliable. Shelter from wet winter winds.
crops.pests: Root rot in wet soil, scale, winter kill in Zone 7 and colder
crops.feeding: Almost none. A little compost in spring is plenty.
careSteps: Plant on a slope or in a pot with grit.
Water only when the top inch is dry.
Harvest sprigs year-round.
Prune after bloom; never cut into old bare wood.

crops.name: Thyme
crops.description: A low, drought-proof mat. The more you pick, the denser it grows.
crops.plantingTips: Plant in spring in grit and sun. Wet winters are the usual killer.
crops.pests: Root rot, spider mites in drought indoors
crops.feeding: No feed. Rich soil makes floppy, flavorless growth.
careSteps: Plant high, on a mound or in a trough.
Shear after flowering.
Harvest in the morning after dew dries.
Replace woody plants every three years.

crops.name: Oregano
crops.description: A sprawling perennial. Flavor peaks just as flower buds form.
crops.plantingTips: Plant in spring. Greek oregano has more bite than common marjoram types.
crops.pests: Aphids, root rot in wet ground
crops.feeding: A light compost mulch in spring only.
careSteps: Plant in full sun.
Pinch to keep it bushy.
Cut flowering stems for drying.
Divide clumps every two years.

crops.name: Dill
crops.description: Feathery annual for leaves and seed heads. Direct-sow; it taproots and hates moving.
crops.plantingTips: Sow where it will stand. Successions every three weeks keep leaf coming.
crops.feeding: No extra feed.
careSteps: Sow directly.
Snip leaves young.
Leave umbels if you want seed and hoverflies.
It self-sows politely.

crops.name: Chives
crops.description: A clump of mild onion greens and edible purple pompoms. Cut and it returns.
crops.plantingTips: Divide a nursery clump in early spring, or sow seed and wait a year for a fat plant.
crops.feeding: Compost in spring. Water in drought or the tips brown.
careSteps: Plant in a clump, not as single leaves.
Cut 2 cm above the soil.
Shear flowers if you want more leaf.
Divide every three years.

crops.name: Sage
crops.description: A grey-leafed perennial with a strong kitchen scent. Woody after a few years.
crops.plantingTips: Plant in spring in a dry, sunny spot. Soft growth from rich soil winters badly.
crops.feeding: No feed. A grit mulch keeps the crown dry.
careSteps: Plant high and dry.
Harvest lightly the first year.
Prune after flowering.
Replace when the center goes woody.

crops.name: Chamomile
crops.description: German chamomile is an annual grown for apple-scented daisy flowers. Roman is a perennial lawn.
crops.plantingTips: Sow German types on the surface — they need light. Thin to sturdy plants.
crops.feeding: No feed. Poor soil makes stronger tea.
careSteps: Surface-sow and press in.
Keep just moist until up.
Pick flowers on a dry morning as they fully open.
Dry in shade on a screen.

crops.name: Sunflower
crops.description: Tall, cheerful annuals that follow the sun. Birds take the seed if you leave heads to dry.
crops.plantingTips: Sow directly after frost, 3 cm deep. Stake tall varieties before the heads fill.
crops.pests: Birds, squirrels, downy mildew, stem borers
crops.feeding: Compost at sowing. Tall types appreciate a potassium feed as buds form.
careSteps: Sow in situ after frost.
Thin to the strongest seedling.
Stake before buds weigh the stem.
Cut for the vase as petals just lift, or leave for seed.

crops.name: Marigold
crops.description: The garden’s pest patrol. French types stay low; African types make big pompoms. Both reseed.
crops.plantingTips: Sow after frost or start indoors. They bloom faster in poor soil than in rich beds.
crops.pests: Slugs on seedlings, spider mites in drought
crops.feeding: No feed. Rich soil makes leaves, not flowers.
careSteps: Sow shallow after frost.
Pinch once to bush out.
Deadhead to keep bloom coming.
Tuck plants among tomatoes and beans.

crops.name: Zinnia
crops.description: Heat-proof cut flowers in every color but blue. The more you cut, the more they branch.
crops.plantingTips: Direct-sow in warm soil. Do not crowd — mildew loves wet zinnia leaves.
crops.feeding: A light compost at sowing. Skip extra nitrogen.
careSteps: Sow after the soil is warm.
Water at the base, not overhead.
Cut stems long for the vase.
Deadhead spent blooms weekly.

crops.name: Cosmos
crops.description: Airy, drought-tough daisies on tall stems. Poor soil makes them flower harder.
crops.plantingTips: Scatter seed on warm, raked ground. Thin so air moves through the stems.
crops.pests: Aphids, cosmos blight in wet summers
crops.feeding: No feed. Fertility makes lanky plants that flop.
careSteps: Sow in situ.
Pinch at 30 cm for branching.
Stake if the site is windy.
Let a few heads seed for next year.

crops.name: Nasturtium
crops.description: Edible leaves, flowers, and seed pods with a pepper bite. A living mulch and aphid decoy.
crops.plantingTips: Sow the large seed 2 cm deep after frost. They bloom better in lean soil.
crops.pests: Aphids (they draw them off other crops), cabbage moth
crops.feeding: None. Feed and you get leaves, not flowers.
careSteps: Nick or soak seed overnight.
Sow after frost.
Pick flowers and leaves for salads.
Harvest green seeds to pickle like capers.

crops.name: Calendula
crops.description: Pot marigold — cool-season daisies used in salves and salads. It shrugs off light frost.
crops.plantingTips: Sow in early spring or autumn. Deadhead or it sets seed and stops blooming.
crops.feeding: No extra feed.
careSteps: Sow as soon as soil can be worked.
Deadhead twice a week.
Pick flowers in the morning for drying.
It self-sows in bare soil.

crops.name: Sweet Pea
crops.description: Fragrant climbers that want a cool start and a tall net. Heat ends the show.
crops.plantingTips: Nick seed and sow in late winter. Pinch once, then keep cutting stems for the house.
crops.companions: Nothing heavy at the roots — give them their own strip
crops.pests: Aphids, powdery mildew, bud drop in heat
crops.feeding: Compost in the trench and a weekly dilute feed once buds show.
careSteps: Soak seed overnight.
Sow deep in cool soil.
Pinch at 10 cm.
Cut every day or they set seed and stop.

crops.name: Dahlia
crops.description: Tuberous showpieces. Lift in cold winters; leave in the ground where frost is light.
crops.plantingTips: Plant tubers when soil is 15°C, eye up, 10 cm deep. Stake at planting, not later.
crops.feeding: Low nitrogen, extra potassium from bud onwards. Too much feed makes weak stems.
careSteps: Plant after frost with a stake in place.
Pinch at 30 cm.
Water deeply once a week.
Lift tubers after the first blackening frost in cold zones.

crops.name: Coneflower
crops.description: Echinacea — a tough prairie perennial. Goldfinches take the seed heads in autumn.
crops.plantingTips: Plant young pots in spring. It flowers more from year two. Leave some heads standing.
crops.pests: Japanese beetles, aster yellows, root rot in wet clay
crops.feeding: Compost in spring. Do not baby it with extra water once established.
careSteps: Plant in spring in a sunny, drained spot.
Water the first summer only.
Cut for the vase or leave for birds.
Divide clumps every four years.

crops.name: Pansy
crops.description: Cool-season faces for beds and pots. They stall in heat and return with autumn.
crops.plantingTips: Set out in late winter. Deadhead or they go to seed and fade.
crops.feeding: A fortnightly dilute feed while blooming.
careSteps: Plant while nights are still cool.
Water evenly.
Pinch faded blooms and seed pods.
Replace or cut back when summer heat arrives.
